verdict.rationale: Crossplane's own reconciliation model runs user-configured function pipelines and automatically corrects drift from desired state, and a real-time compositions flag hints at reacting to resource changes. That makes it a declarative, reconciliation-driven take on automatic actions rather than an explicit event-rule engine. missing for 10: documented user-defined event-trigger rules (event → action), a description of what real-time compositions actually react to, examples of event-driven workflows, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Instead you configure a pipeline of functions. The functions return declarative configuration that Crossplane should apply.
If your software ever drifts from your desired state, the control plane automatically corrects the drift.
`--enable-realtime-compositions` Enable support for real time compositions.
